# The koto floor. /deliver enters its session through
# skills/deliver/scripts/deliver-open.sh and the shared scripts/koto-open.sh,
# which is the call site for `koto init --vars-file`, `--attach-live`,
# `--replace-terminal` and `--koto-leg`. Those flags exist only from the koto
# release .tsuku.toml pins, and so do everything deliver.md is built from:
# request-leg gates, transition context_assignments reading a leg's payload,
# result maps, constrained variables, and `overridable: false` gates. So the
# `koto init` record below, with the same flags /scope and /execute declare, is
# /deliver's declared koto floor: the tool-declaration policy allows no version
# number here, and preflight on an older koto names these missing flags and
# the install route before any work starts. The one-directional requires check
# does not look for them in this skill's own files, because the call site is
# the shared script.
# The request verbs are /deliver's one write of its own, the per-run koto
# request, and the reads of it. deliver-open-request.sh (open_request's
# default action) lists this topic's open requests with `request list
# --coordinator-of-record --state`, abandons each with `request
# abandon-request --rationale`, and creates this run's with `request create
# --with-data --requested-by --coordinator-of-record`. deliver-absent.sh
# (scope_absent and execute_absent) records the fixed child-absent result with
# `request resolve --with-data` and reads the leg back with `request get`.
# SKILL.md closes the run's request on the way out with `request close`, after
# finding it with `request list`. The leg gates read the request inside koto
# and need no verb.
# The session: every tick is `koto next --no-cleanup` (evidence with
# --with-data), the report reads `koto status`, deliver-open.sh removes this
# worktree's earlier deliver-<topic> with `koto session cleanup`, and
# deliver-probe.sh writes its verdicts with `koto context add` after clearing
# them with `koto context remove`.
